ITQAN:v4p427/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p427/r10.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
ITQAN:v4p427/r10.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī says no verse is more hopeful for this community than the verse about people who confess their sins and mix good deeds with bad.
ITQAN:v4p427/r10.anchor: عن أبي عثمان النهدي قال ما في القرآن آية أرجى عندي لهذه الأمة من قوله ﴿ وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم

ITQAN:v4p387/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p387/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p387/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the penitents as seven people, Abū Lubāba and his companions.
ITQAN:v4p387/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس هم سبعة أبو لبابة وأصحابه

ITQAN:v4p387/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p387/r7.speaker: قتادة
ITQAN:v4p387/r7.claim: Qatāda names seven Anṣār among the penitents: Abū Lubāba, al-Jadd b. Qays, Khidhām, Aws, Kardam, and Mirdās.
ITQAN:v4p387/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة سبعة من الأنصار أبو لبابة وجد بن قيس وخذام وأوس وكردم ومرداس

ITQAN:v3p171/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p171/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p171/r3.claim: A preposition and its object are omitted: they mixed righteous work with bad work, and bad work with righteous work.
ITQAN:v3p171/r3.anchor: حذف الجار مع المجرور ﴿ خلطوا عملا صالحا ﴾

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r11.claim: The confession verse is said to concern ten men who stayed behind from Tabūk; reports vary on whether ten, eight, seven, six, five, or three were involved and who bound themselves in the mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r11.anchor: نزلت في عشرة رهط تخلفوا عن غزوة تبوك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r12.claim: One report names three who tied themselves to the mosque pillars: Abū Lubāba, Aws ibn Thaʿlaba, and Wadīʿa ibn Khidhām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r12.anchor: ثلاثة أبو لبابة بن عبد المنذر، وأوس بن ثعلبة، ووديعة بن خذام الأنصاري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r13.claim: The report that the verse concerned only Abū Lubāba is unlikely because the wording ‘others’ is plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r13.anchor: ويبعد ذلك من لفظ وآخرون، لأنه جمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r14.claim: On the Prophet’s return, the bound men said they would remain tied until he released them; he also swore to wait for revelation, then released and excused them after the verse came down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p497#2/r14.anchor: رغبوا عني، وتخلفوا عن الغزو مع المسلمين» فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the verse concerns Abū Lubāba’s advice to Banū Qurayẓa to surrender, signaling with his throat that the Prophet would execute them; he repented and bound himself to a mosque pillar until forgiven.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نزلت في أبي لبابة في شأنه مع بني قريظة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r2.claim: The men’s confession is an admission of sin; the good deed is repentance and remorse, while the bad deed is their failure to join the expedition or, in another account, their earlier departure for jihad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r2.anchor: والاعتراف: الإقرار بالذنب عملا صالحا توبة وندما، وآخر سيئا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r3.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the bad deed as staying behind from this expedition; al-Ḥasan and others also contrast prior jihad with this absence, while al-Kalbī says it means repentance mixed with sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r3.anchor: أي تخلفا عن هذه الغزاة قاله: الطبري، أو خروجا إلى الجهاد قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that coordinating the two deeds makes each one both mixed and mixed-with, unlike saying water was mixed into milk, which marks only the water as mixed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r4.anchor: وعطف أحدهما على الآخر دليل على أن كل واحد منهما مخلوط ومخلوط به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also compares the construction to ‘I sold the sheep, a sheep and a dirham,’ meaning a sheep for a dirham.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من قولهم: بعت الشاء شاة ودرهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ‘perhaps’ is certain when spoken by God; Abū Ḥayyān says its tentative wording leaves believers in hope and apprehension before concluding with forgiveness and mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: عسى من الله واجب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r7.claim: Although revealed about particular men, the verse applies generally to the Muslim community until the Resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية وإن نزلت في ناس. مخصوصين فهي عامة في الأمة إلى يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r8.speaker: أبو عثمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r8.claim: Abū ʿUthmān considers this among the most hope-giving verses in the Qur’an for the community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان: ما في القرآن آية أرجى عندي لهذه الأمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r9.claim: A Bayhaqī account of the Ascension shows repentant people who mixed good and bad deeds around Abraham, their colors cleansed by bathing in three rivers before rejoining white-faced companions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p498/r9.anchor: وفي حديث الإسراء والمعراج من تخريج البيهقي: أن الذين خلطوا عملا صالحا

DURR-FULL:v4p276/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r2.claim: The confession of sin concerns Abu Lubaba, who warned Qurayza of slaughter by gesturing across his throat when they asked about surrendering to Muhammad's judgment.
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فاعترفوا بذنبهم} قال: هو أبو لبابة إذ قال لقريظة ما قال

DURR-FULL:v4p276/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r3.claim: Banu Qurayza, allies of Abu Lubaba, asked whether he advised surrender; he signaled that it meant death, and the Prophet rebuked him for thinking God had overlooked the gesture.
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r3.anchor: أن بني قريظة كانوا حلفاء لأبي لبابة فاطلعوا إليه وهو يدعوهم إلى حكم رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v4p276/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r4.claim: After returning from Tabuk, Abu Lubaba was shunned, bound himself to a pillar for seven days without food or water, and remained until God announced his repentance.
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r4.anchor: فارتبط بسارية التوبة التي عند باب أم سلمة سبعا بين يوم وليلة في حر شديد لا يأكل فيهن ولا يشرب

DURR-FULL:v4p276/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r5.claim: After release, Abu Lubaba vowed to leave his home and donate his property; the Prophet said donating one third would suffice.
DURR-FULL:v4p276/r5.anchor: وإني أختلع من مالي صدقة إلى الله ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يجزي عنك الثلث

DURR-FULL:v4p277/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r2.claim: Those who confessed their sins were eight people who tied themselves to pillars, including Kardam, Mirdas, and Abu Lubaba.
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم} قال: هم الثمانية الذين ربطوا أنفسهم بالسواري

DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.claim: Seven stayed behind at Tabuk; four mixed good and bad deeds—Jadd ibn Qays, Abu Lubaba, Haram, and Aws—and they were pardoned and ordered to give charity.
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} قال: ذكر لنا أنهم كانوا سبعة رهط

DURR-FULL:v4p277/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r4.claim: He identifies their good deed as campaigning with the Prophet and their bad deed as staying behind.
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r4.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} قال: غزوهم مع رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v4p277/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r5.claim: He calls the verse about people confessing mixed deeds the most hope-giving verse in the Qur'an for this community.
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r5.anchor: عن أبي عثمان النهدي قال: ما في القرآن آية أرجى عندي لهذه الأمة

DURR-FULL:v4p277/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r6.speaker: مطرف
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r6.claim: He compares himself with the Qur'an's descriptions of devoted night worshippers and Hell's inmates, finding himself in neither group and hoping instead to belong among those with mixed deeds.
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r6.anchor: عن مطرف قال: إني لاستلقي من الليل على فراشي وأتدبر القرآن فأعرض أعمالي

DURR-FULL:v4p278/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r1.claim: Jabir names six who stayed behind at Tabuk: Abu Lubaba, Aws ibn Judham, Tha'laba ibn Wadi'a, Ka'b ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayya.
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: كان ممن تخلف عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك ستة

DURR-FULL:v4p278/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r2.claim: Abu Lubaba, Aws, and Tha'laba tied themselves to pillars and offered their wealth; the Prophet said he would not release them until there was fighting, and verse 9:102 was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r2.anchor: فربطوا أنفسهم بالسواري وجاؤوا بأموالهم فقالوا: يا رسول الله خذ هذا الذي حبسنا عنك

DURR-FULL:v4p278/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r4.speaker: الأحنف بن قيس
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r4.claim: He says he found no verse more resembling his own condition than the one about confessing mixed deeds.
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r4.anchor: عن ابن شوذب قال: قال الأحنف بن قيس: عرضت نفسي على القرآن فلم أجدني بآية أشبه مني

DURR-FULL:v4p278/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r5.claim: Hasan says the repentants did repent and that God's statement that He may accept repentance is a certainty.
DURR-FULL:v4p278/r5.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار قال: سألت الحسن عن قول الله {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} فقال: يا مالك تابوا

SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r1.claim: آخرون may coordinate with منافقون, meaning other hypocrites among those around the audience or among Medina's people.
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وآخرون }: نسق على " منافقون " أي: وممن حولكم آخرون، أو ومن أهل المدينة آخرون

SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r2.claim: Alternatively, آخرون is a subject, اعترفوا its adjective, and خلطوا its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مبتدأ و " اعترفوا " صفته، والخبر قوله " خلطوا "

SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says each deed is mixed with the other; unlike خلطت الماء باللبن, the waw presents both as mixed and as what the other is mixed with.
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: قد جعل كل واحد منهما مخلوطا فما المخلوط به؟ قلت: كل واحد مخلوط ومخلوط به،

SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares بعت الشاء شاة ودرهما, meaning a sheep for a dirham; the author clarifies he paraphrases the meaning, not that waw means bāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r4.anchor: ثم قال: " ويجوز أن يكون من قولهم: " بعت الشاء: شاة ودرهما " بمعنى: شاة بدرهم " قلت:

SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa notes that خلطت الحنطة والشعير is also possible even with bāʾ, as in خلطت الحنطة بالشعير.
SAMIN-DURR:9:102/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " ولو كان بالباء جاز أن تقول: خلطت الحنطة والشعير،

SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r1.claim: عسى الله may be independent or the predicate of آخرون; in the latter analysis خلطوا is a circumstantial clause with an implied قد.
SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الجملة مستأنفة، ويجوز أن تكون في محل رفع خبرا ل " آخرون " ، ويكون قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r2.claim: The author summarizes three analyses: آخرون coordinates with منافقون, or is a subject predicated by خلطوا or by the hopeful clause عسى الله.
SAMIN-DURR:9:102#2/r2.anchor: فتلخص في " آخرون " أنه معطوف على " منافقون " ، أو مبتدأ مخبر عنه ب " خلطوا "

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n135/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n135/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n135/r1.claim: These people are neither full believers nor hypocrites, but hesitant and confused between right and wrong or truth and falsehood.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n135/r1.anchor: half-hearted, confused waverers between right and wrong, or between truth and falsehood

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r1.claim: Asad glosses the phrase as confessing sins after mixing a righteous deed with an evil one.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r1.anchor: who have acknowledged their sins [after] having mingled a righteous deed with another that was evil

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r2.claim: The verse primarily concerns wavering Muslims who stayed behind from the Tabuk expedition.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r2.anchor: vacillating Muslims who refused to participate in the expedition to Tabuk

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r3.claim: More broadly, it applies to any sinners who recognize and repent of wrongdoing without outside prompting.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n136/r3.anchor: all sinners who - without external prompting - become conscious of their wrongdoing and repent of it.

IBNHISHAM:v2p238/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p238/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
IBNHISHAM:v2p238/r1.claim: Some learned authorities say Abū Lubāba remained tied to a tree trunk for six nights; his wife untied him for each prayer and bound him again. The verse is identified as revealed about his repentance.
IBNHISHAM:v2p238/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام: أقام أبو لبابة مرتبطا بالجذع ست ليال. تأتيه امرأته في كل وقت صلاة

IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r4.claim: The confessing sinners are mentioned after the hypocrites and before the command to take alms from them.
IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r4.anchor: ثم قال تعالى: وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم، خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا، عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r1.claim: Qatada identifies these as people who stayed behind from the Tabuk campaign, including Abu Lubaba and Judd ibn Qays; they later repented, and Qatada distinguishes them from the three.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا ﴾ قال هم نفر ممن تخلف عن غزوة تبوك منهم أبو لبابة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r2.speaker: الزهري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri recounts that Abu Lubaba, who stayed behind at Tabuk, bound himself to a pillar and fasted seven days until God accepted his repentance; the Prophet freed him, then limited his proposed charity to one-third of his wealth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p286#3/r2.anchor: عن الزهري قال كان أبو لبابة ممن تخلف عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك قال الزهري فربط نفسه بسارية

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r1.claim: In Ibn Masʿūd's Badr report, Abu Bakr urges sparing the captives in hope that God accepts their repentance, echoing 9:102's hope for penitents.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3632/r1.anchor: فقال أبو بكر: يا رسول الله، قومك وأهلك، استبقهم، واستأن بهم، لعل الله أن يتوب عليهم،

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r1.claim: The “others” are Muslims of weak religious resolve, not hypocrites, according to the preferred view; another view says they were hypocrites whom God enabled to repent.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r1.anchor: بيان لحال طائفة من المسلمين ضعيفة الهمم في أمر الدين ولم يكونوا منافقين على الصحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r2.claim: One parsing makes “others” the subject, “they mixed” a circumstantial clause with qad understood, and “perhaps God will turn to them” the predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r2.anchor: قيل : وهو مبتدأ خبره جملة ( خلطوا ) وهي حال بتقدير قد

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r3.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r3.claim: The more exact grammarians coordinate “others” with the preceding “hypocrites”: another group among those around Medina or its residents.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r3.anchor: والمحققون على أنه معطوف على ( منافقون ) أي ومنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r4.claim: They knowingly acknowledged staying behind the campaign, preferring ease, and accepting bad company with hypocrites; they did not make false excuses reinforced by false oaths.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r4.anchor: أقروا عن معرفة ( بذنوبهم ( التي هي تخلفهم عن الغزو

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqī and others report from Ibn ʿAbbās that ten stayed behind at Tabūk; seven tied themselves to mosque pillars, including Abū Lubāba and companions, and vowed not to untie until the Prophet released them. He vowed not to release or excuse them until God did; revelation followed, and he freed and excused them.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما عشرة تخلفوا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r6.claim: Reports differ on the number: another Ibn ʿAbbās account says three, Ibn Abī Ḥātim's report from Zayd says eight, and other reports say five; all include Abū Lubāba ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r6.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه أنهم كانوا ثلاثة وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن زيد أنهم كانوا ثمانية

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r7.speaker: الحسن والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī identify the good deed as going out to jihad with the Prophet and the bad as staying behind.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says the first deed is repentance and the second is sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r8.anchor: وعن الكلبي أن الأول التوبة والثاني الإثم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r9.claim: Another view takes the good deed as all righteous conduct and the bad as its opposite.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : العمل الصالح يعم جميع البر والطاعة والسيء ماكان ضده

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r10.claim: Khalṭ means blending and implies both something blended and what it is blended with.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r10.anchor: والخلط المزيج وهو يستدعي مخلوطا ومخلوطا به

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r11.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r11.claim: Sībawayh is cited for treating wāw as bāʾ in an expression like “I sold the sheep, one sheep and a dirham”; this is a metaphor of accompaniment.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r11.anchor: كما نقل عن سيبويه في قولهم : بعت الشاء شاة ودرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r12.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r12.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib reconstructs the example as “I sold the sheep for one dirham,” with wāw replacing accompaniment-bāʾ; al-Ālūsī calls this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r12.anchor: عن ابن الحاجب إن أصل المثال بعت الشاء شاة بدرهم أي مع درهم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says each deed is both blended and a blending agent, as in reciprocal mixing of water and milk; wāw conveys two mixings, more emphatically than “mixed one with the other.”
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r13.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري أن كل واحد من المتعاطفين مخلوط ومخلوط به

ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r14.claim: With wāw, context makes each deed both what is mixed and what mixes the other, yielding two reciprocal blendings rather than the single blending expressed by bāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p11#2/r14.anchor: وحاصله أن المخلوط به في كل واحد من الخلطين هو المخلوط في الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r1.claim: Mixing one thing into another does not entail reciprocal mixing; the objection conflates mixing with mutual intermixture.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r1.anchor: والحق أن إختلاط أحد الشيئين بالآخر مستلزم لإختلاط الآخر به وأما خلط أحدهما بالآخر فلا يستلزم خلط الآخر به

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r2.claim: Alusi favors al-Sakkaki's two sequences of good then bad and bad then good over al-Zamakhshari's apparent identity of the acts, but rejects annulment as Mu'tazilite.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r2.anchor: وكلام الزمخشري ظاهر في إتحادهما وفيه مافيه ولذلك رجح ما ذهب إليه السكاكي لكن ماذكره من الإحباط ميل إلى مذهب المعتزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r3.claim: Some posit an omitted reciprocal construction, but Alusi calls that ellipsis contrary to the apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r3.anchor: نوع من البديع يسمى الإحتباك والأصل خلطوا عملا صالحا بآخر سيء

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r4.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r4.claim: Ibn al-Munir takes mixing to imply doing, as if the verse said they did good and bad deeds, with the preposition omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r4.anchor: واستظهر ابن المنير كون الخلط مضمنا معنى العمل والعدول عن الباء

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r5.claim: Alusi takes mixing as bringing together; in context, the good is admitting sins for missing the expedition, and the bad is those sins, with confession foremost.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r5.anchor: وأنا أختار أن الخلط بمعنى الجميع هنا وإذا إعتبر السياق وسبب النزول

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r6.claim: Without relying on the occasion, good may be confession of sins generally and bad the sins themselves, or good and bad deeds generally, with good foregrounded as opening reform.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يراد من العمل الصالح الإعتراف بالذنوب مطلقا ومن السيء الذنوب كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r7.claim: A saying cited urges following a bad deed with a good one, which erases it; no authority is named.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r7.anchor: ففي الخبر أتبع السيئة بالحسنة تمحها

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r8.speaker: الأسود بن قيس
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r8.claim: Ibn Sa'd reports Aswad ibn Qays's account of Hasan ibn Ali telling Habib ibn Maslama that serving Mu'awiya for worldly gain damaged his religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن سعد عن الأسود بن قيس قال : لقي الحسن بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r9.speaker: مطرف
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r9.claim: Matruf compares himself with worshippers of Paradise and people destined for Saqar, then hopes he and his listeners belong among those who confessed sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r9.anchor: عن مطرف قال : إني لأستلقي من الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r10.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r10.claim: Abu Uthman al-Nahdi says no Qur'anic verse gives him more hope for this community than this one.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r10.anchor: عن أبي عثمان النهدي قال : مافي القرآن آية أرجى عندي لهذه الأمة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r11.claim: Alusi reads the hopeful reports as resting on God's promised acceptance, not necessarily prior repentance; he considers 39:53 still more hopeful.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p12/r11.anchor: والظاهر أنه لم يفهم منها صدور التوبة من هؤلاء الآخرين بل ثبت لهم الحكم المفهوم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r1.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r1.claim: Several interpreters infer repentance from confession because the two are customarily associated.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r1.anchor: وجعل غير واحد الإعتراف دالا على التوبة ولعل ذلك لما بينهما من اللزوم عرفا

ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r2.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r2.claim: Al-Shihab says confession counts as repentance when joined to regret and resolve not to repeat the sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r2.anchor: وقال الشهاب : لأنه توبة إذا إقترن بالندم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r3.claim: Alusi objects that general wording cannot imply this particular condition by any of the three recognized modes of indication.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر أن العام لا يدل على الخاص بإحدى الدلالات الثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r4.claim: Although asa ordinarily expresses hope, from the Most Generous it amounts to a promise and certain acceptance of repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r4.anchor: عسى للأطماع وهو من أكرم الأكرمين إيجاب وأي إيجاب

ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r5.claim: God's abundant forgiveness and mercy explain acceptance of the penitent as gracious commitment, not an obligation imposed on God as the Mu'tazilites maintain.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p13/r5.anchor: تعليل لما أفادته من وجوب القبول وليس هو الوجوب الذي يقوله المعتزلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r1.claim: These are some of those who stayed behind, who admitted their sins instead of making false excuses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r1.anchor: ولم يعتذروا عن تخلفهم بالمعاذير الكاذبة، وهم طائفة من المتخلفين

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r2.claim: A report says they tied themselves to pillars in the mosque after learning what had been revealed about those who stayed behind. The Prophet saw them after his customary prayer, heard they would not release themselves until he did, swore he would wait for a command about them, then the verse came and he released them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r2.anchor: أوثقوا أنفسهم على سواري المسجد لما بلغهم ما نزل في المتخلفين

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r3.claim: Their good deed was showing regret and confessing sin; their bad deed was staying behind and siding with hypocrites.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r3.anchor: الفعل الصالح الذي هو إظهار الندم والاعتراف بالذنب بآخر سيء هو التخلف وموافقة أهل النفاق

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r4.claim: The conjunction wāw may mean biʾ, as in the idiom of selling a sheep for a sheep and a dirham, or show that each act is mixed with the other.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r4.anchor: والواو إما بمعنى الباء كما في قولهم بعت الشاء شاة ودرهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r5.claim: God may accept their repentance, which is indicated by their confession of their sins.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r5.anchor: أن يقبل توبتهم وهي مدلول عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:102/r6.claim: God overlooks the penitent's sins and graciously favors the penitent.

BURSEVI:v3p373#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p373#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p373#3/r3.claim: The other people mentioned are another group from among the people of Medina.
BURSEVI:v3p373#3/r3.anchor: {وءاخرون} أي : ومن أهل المدينة قوم آخرون

BURSEVI:v3p374/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374/r1.claim: They admitted staying behind, preferring ease, and accepting proximity to hypocrites; they regretted it and offered no false excuses.
BURSEVI:v3p374/r1.anchor: التي هي تخلفهم عن العفو وإيثار الدعة عليه والرضى بسوء جوار المنافقين

BURSEVI:v3p374/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374/r2.claim: A group of those who stayed behind tied themselves to mosque pillars and swore not to unbind until the Prophet released them; after returning, he prayed two rakʿas, heard their case, awaited revelation, then freed and excused them.
BURSEVI:v3p374/r2.anchor: فعاهدوا الله وأقسموا أن لا يطلقوا أنفسهم حتى يكون رسول الله هو الذي يطلقهم

BURSEVI:v3p374/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374/r3.claim: Their good deeds were earlier righteous works and prior campaigns, together with their present confession, remorse, and regret for missing this expedition.
BURSEVI:v3p374/r3.anchor: هو ما سبق منهم من الأعمال الصالحة والخروج إلى المغازي السابق وما لحق من الاعتراف بذنوبهم في التخلف عن هذه المرة وتذممهم وندامتهم

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r1.claim: The bad deed was their earlier and later misconduct, including staying behind from the Tabuk expedition.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r1.anchor: هو ما صدر عنهم من الأعمال السيئة أولا وآخرا فيدخل فيه التخلف عن غزو تبوك

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r2.claim: Using conjunction waw rather than preposition bāʾ presents the good and bad deeds as mutually mixed; bāʾ would imply one is mixed into the other, while waw assigns no direction.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r2.anchor: وتبديل الواو بالباء حيث لم يقل بآخر يؤذن بكون كل منهما مخلوطا به

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r3.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r3.claim: Al-Haddadi says they went to jihad on one occasion and stayed back on another, combining good and bad deeds as one combines coins or water and milk.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r3.anchor: قال الحدادي : يقال خرجوا إلى الجهاد مرة وتخلفوا مرة فجمعوا بين العمل الصالح والعمل السيء

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r4.claim: God's turning toward them means accepting the repentance implied by their confession of sins.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r4.anchor: أن يقبل توبتهم المفهومة من اعترافهم بذنوبهم

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r5.claim: God overlooks the repenter's sins and grants grace; this explains the hope expressed by ʿasā, which from the Most Generous amounts to an assurance of acceptance.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r5.anchor: يتجاوز عن سيئات التائب ويتفضل عليه وهو تعليل لما يفيده كلمة عسى من وجوب القبول

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r6.speaker: أدى
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r6.claim: The word ʿasā keeps a person between hope and apprehension, making reliance and neglect less likely.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r6.anchor: قال أدى وإنما ذكر لفظ عسى ليكون الإنسان بين الطمع والإشفاق فيكون أبعد من الاتكال والإهمال

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r7.claim: A Persian couplet warns that confessing a sin turns one away from it, while refusing to own one's sin signals eternal misery.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r7.anchor: ون بدى كناهرا دانى كشدت جانب شيمانى ورندانى كنا هراكه بدست آن نشان شقاوت ابدست

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r8.claim: The nafs has hypocritical animal desire that discipline can subdue but not erase, unbelieving beastly appetite required by bodily nourishment, and believing predatory or satanic traits that can turn into virtues through Islam and faith.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r8.anchor: اعلم أن بعض النفوس منافق وبعضها كافر وبعضها مؤمن فالمنافق منها كالصفة الحيوانية من الشهوات فإنها تتبدل بالعفة عند استيلاء القلب على النفس

BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r9.claim: The Prophet calls lying, betrayal of trust, breaking promises, and treachery signs of hypocrisy; even one trait remains hypocrisy until abandoned, despite prayer and fasting.
BURSEVI:v3p374#2/r9.anchor: جعل النبي عليه السلام الكذب والخيانة وخلف الوعد والغدر من النفاق

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says ten men stayed behind from Tabuk; seven bound themselves to the mosque pillars, and when the Prophet returned he delayed releasing or excusing them until God did so, after which the verse was revealed and they were released.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا واخر سيئا قال : كان عشرة رهط تخلفوا عن النبي

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r2.speaker: زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r2.claim: Eight men tied themselves to pillars, including Kurdum, Mirdas, and Abu Lubaba; after their release the Prophet was asked to take charity from their property.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r2.anchor: عن زيد واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا واخر سيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Abu Lubaba and two men regretted staying in comfort while the Prophet and believers fought; they bound themselves, and the Prophet awaited God's command to release and excuse them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1872/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا واخر سيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r1.claim: One account says seven stayed behind at Tabuk and four mixed good and bad deeds: Jad ibn Qays, Abu Lubaba, Khidham, and Aws, all Ansar.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا واخر سيئا قال : ذكر لنا انهم كانوا سبعة رهط

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r2.claim: A second account says they were some who stayed behind at Tabuk, including Abu Lubaba and Jad ibn Qays, and that God pardoned them; Qatada says they were not three.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r2.anchor: عن قتادة واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا واخر سيئا قال : هم نفر ممن تخلف عن تبوك

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r3.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about one man, Abu Lubaba.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم نزلت في رجل واحد في ابي لبابة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies Abu Lubaba's sin as signaling to Qurayza that Muhammad would slaughter them if they submitted to his judgment.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم : أبو لبابة حين قال : لقريظة ماقال اشار بيده الى حلقه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the people as Bedouins.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم قال : هم من الاعراب

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r6.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that on the Night Journey he saw two groups of his community, one in paper-white garments and one in grey; Gabriel said the grey-clad people had mixed good and evil deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : قلنا : يارسول الله ثنا مارايت ليلة اسرى بك ؟ قال : رايت امتي ضربين ضرب عليهم ثياب اشد بياضا من القرطاس

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r7.speaker: الأحنف بن قيس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r7.claim: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays says he found no Qur'anic verse that resembled him more than this one.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1873/r7.anchor: قال الاحنف بن قيس : عرضت نفسي علي القران فلم اجدني باية اشبه مني بهذه الاية : واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r1.claim: Al-Suddi identifies their good deed as campaigning alongside the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r1.anchor: عن السدي قوله واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا واخر سيئا والصالح غزوهم مع النبي

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains their acknowledgment of their sins as their repentance.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : واعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا واخر سيئا قال : تابوا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the evil deed as staying behind from the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r3.anchor: عن السدي قوله واخر سيئا قال : السئ : تخلفه عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك، الحسن، أبو مالك، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that God's “perhaps” is certain; the same view is reported from al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : عسى الله ان يتوب عليهم وعسى من الله واجب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r1.claim: Most likely, this sentence coordinates with “among those around you” in 9:101: alongside nearby Bedouin hypocrites were Medinans who had sinned through staying behind and confessed; plural sins and mixed deeds mark believers, not hypocrites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r1.anchor: الأظهر أن جملة : { وءاخرون اعترفوا } عطف على جملة : { وممن حولكم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r2.claim: Among them were al-Jadd ibn Qays, Kardam, Aras ibn Tha'laba, Wadi'a ibn Hizam, Mirdas, Abu Qays, and Abu Lubaba, with three others; after staying behind from Tabuk, they repented and tied themselves to mosque pillars until this verse revealed God's pardon.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r2.anchor: وكان من هؤلاء جماعة منهم الجد بن قيس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r3.claim: I'tiraf derives from ʿarafa and intensifies knowing, hence admission and no longer denying; confession of a past sin implies regret and resolve not to repeat it, though withdrawal from a past act is impossible.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r4.claim: Their good deeds were mixed with the wrongs of staying behind from the campaign and failing to contribute expenditure for the army.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#2/r4.anchor: وخلطهم العمل الصالح والسيىء هو خلطهم حسنات أعمالهم بسيئات التخلف عن الغزو وعدم الإنفاق على الجيش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r1.claim: Coordinating the two objects with waw treats them equally as participants in mixing; the alternative “mixing one with the other” means the same, but the coordinated wording is clearer and more eloquent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r1.anchor: جاء ذكر الشيئين المختلطين بالعطف بالواو على اعتبار استوائهما في وقوع فعل الخلط عليهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r2.claim: As God's words to the Prophet, “perhaps” is a metonym for assured fulfillment—God has accepted their repentance—while retaining the nuance of the speaker's choice about whether it occurs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r2.anchor: وهي من كلام الله تعالى المخاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهي كناية عن وقوع المرجو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r3.claim: God's turning to them means accepting their repentance, as Ibn Ashur discussed at 2:37.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r3.anchor: ومعنى : { أن يتوب عليهم } أي يقبل توبتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r4.claim: The closing statement that God is forgiving and merciful is a coda well suited to this context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p21#3/r4.anchor: إن الله غفور رحيم } تذييل مناسب للمقام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r1.claim: One account from Ibn ʿAbbās says ten men stayed behind at Tabūk; as the Prophet neared return, seven bound themselves to mosque pillars and vowed not to free themselves until he did. He initially refused, then the verse was revealed and he released and excused them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r1.anchor: أنهم عشرة رهط تخلفوا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك فلما دنا رجوع رسول الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r2.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās says six stayed behind: Abū Lubāba and two others bound themselves, while three did not; after revelation the Prophet released and excused them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r2.anchor: وروى العوفي عن ابن عباس أن الذين تخلفوا كانوا ستة فأوثق أبو لبابة نفسه ورجلان معه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r3.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the three were Abū Lubāba ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir, Aws ibn Thaʿlaba, and Wadīʿa ibn Khidhām al-Anṣārī.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r3.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس أنهم كانوا ثلاثة أبو لبابة بن عبد المنذر وأوس ابن ثعلبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وزيد بن أسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, and Zayd ibn Aslam say the group comprised eight men.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وزيد ابن أسلم كانوا ثمانية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says it was reported that they were seven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة ذكر لنا أنهم كانوا سبعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r6.claim: A second occasion-of-revelation view says the verse concerned Abū Lubāba alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r6.anchor: والثاني أنها نزلت في أبي لبانه وحده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid says Abū Lubāba’s sin was betraying God and His Messenger by signaling to Banū Qurayẓa that Saʿd’s judgment meant slaughter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r7.anchor: أنه خان الله ورسوله باشارته إلى بني قريظة حين شاوروه في النزول على حكم سعد أنه الذبح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r8.speaker: الزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r8.claim: Al-Zuhrī says Abū Lubāba’s sin was staying behind from the Tabūk campaign.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r8.anchor: والثاني أنه تخلفه عن تبوك قاله الزهري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r9.claim: Iʿtirāf is admitting something with knowledge; confessing sin better demonstrates truthful repentance and acceptance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p493#2/r9.anchor: فأما الاعتراف فهو الاقرار بالشيء عن معرفة والاعتراف بالذنب أدعى إلى صدق التوبة والقبول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r1.claim: Ibn Jarīr says the wāw stands in place of bāʾ, so the sense is that they mixed a good deed with an evil one, as one mixes water and milk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r1.anchor: قال ابن جرير وضع الواو مكان الباء والمعنى بآخر سيء كما تقول خلطت الماء واللبن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r2.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the good deed as their earlier jihad and the evil deed as their later failure to join the campaign.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r2.anchor: أن العمل الصالح ما سبق من جهادهم والسيء التأخر عن الجهاد قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ identifies their repentance as the good deed and their staying behind as the evil deed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r3.anchor: أن العمل الصالح توبتهم والسيء تخلفهم ذكره الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says عسى here expresses a promise that God will certainly accept their repentance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنه واجب من الله تعالى قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r5.claim: Another view keeps them between hope and apprehension, which discourages heedlessness and neglect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495/r5.anchor: أنه ترديد لهم بين الطمع والإشفاق وذلك يصد عن اللهو والإهمال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r1.claim: After describing hypocrites who stayed from campaigns through aversion, denial, and doubt, the passage turns to sinners who stayed from laziness and comfort despite believing the truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r1.anchor: لما بين تعالى حال المنافقين المتخلفين عن الغزاة رغبة عنها وتكذيبا وشكا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r2.claim: They admitted their sins to God and mixed good deeds with bad; they remain under God’s pardon and forgiveness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r2.anchor: أقروا بها واعترفوا فيما بينهم وبين ربهم، ولهم أعمال أخر صالحة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r3.claim: Although the verse was revealed about particular people, Ibn Kathir says its scope includes all sincere, erring sinners who are tainted by wrongdoing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية -وإن كانت نزلت في أناس معينين -إلا أنها عامة في كل المذنبين الخاطئين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r4.claim: Mujahid says the verse was revealed about Abu Lubabah, who signaled to Banu Qurayzah that the outcome for them was slaughter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r4.anchor: في أبي لبابة لما قال لبني قريظة: إنه الذبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerned Abu Lubabah and companions who stayed behind from Tabuk; accounts differ whether five, seven, or nine joined him. They bound themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet released and pardoned them after revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: {وآخرون} نزلت في أبي لبابة وجماعة من أصحابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r6.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r6.claim: In a dream report narrated by Samurah ibn Jundub, the Prophet sees a mixed-appearance group transformed after bathing in a river; angels identify them as people who mixed good and evil deeds, whom God forgave. Al-Bukhari gives it in abbreviated form here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p206/r6.anchor: حدثنا سمرة بن جندب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا: "أتاني الليلة آتيان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies them as seven Ansar, including Abu Lubaba ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir, Aws ibn Thaʿlaba, and Wadiʿa ibn Hizam, among those who stayed behind at Tabuk. Regretting this, they tied themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet returned and God revealed the verse; he then released them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the person as Abu Lubaba alone, who warned Banu Qurayza that the Prophet would kill them if they submitted to his judgment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r2.anchor: إنه ذابحكم إن نزلتم على حكمه , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r3.claim: Al-Suddi takes the good deed as jihad and the bad deed as staying behind from it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r3.anchor: أحدها : أن الصالح : الجهاد , والسيء , التأخر عنه , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r4.speaker: بعض التابعين
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r4.claim: Some Successors take the bad deed as sin and the good deed as repentance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r4.anchor: الثاني : أن السيىء : الذنب والصالح : التوبة , قاله بعض التابعين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398/r5.claim: Al-Hasan expresses the mixture in a rhymed contrast: a sin and a lash, not abundant gold or something dropped away.

MUJAHID:v1p286/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p286/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p286/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the one who confessed as Abu Lubaba, who signaled to Qurayza at his throat that Muhammad would slaughter them if they submitted to his judgment.
MUJAHID:v1p286/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ اعترفوا بذنوبهم ﴾ قال هو قول أبي لبابة إذ قال لقريظة ما قال واشار إلى حلقه بأن محمد يذبحكم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r1.claim: These were another group who, unlike others, made no false excuses for staying behind but confessed their fault and regretted it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r1.anchor: لم يعتذروا من تخلفهم بالمعاذير الكاذبة كغيرهم ولكن اعترفوا على أنفسهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r2.claim: The source reports that seven of ten tied themselves up; after returning and praying, the Prophet waited for God's command, released them after revelation, declined their offered wealth, and then 9:103 was revealed.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r2.anchor: وكانوا عشرة فسبعة منهم لما بلغهم ما نزل فى المتخلفين أوثقوا أنفسهم على سوارى المسجد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r3.claim: The good deed may mean going out for jihad, with the bad deed meaning staying behind; alternatively, they mixed repentance with sin.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r3.anchor: خروجا إلى الجهاد ﴿ وآخر سيئا ﴾ تخلفا عنه أو التوبة والاثم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r4.claim: The conjunction wāw may carry the sense of bāʾ because conjunction and attachment are compatible.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r4.anchor: فالواو بمعنى الباء لأن الواو للجمع والباء للالصاق فيتناسبان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, the wāw means each deed was mixed with the other, unlike saying water was mixed with milk, which makes only the water mixed into the milk.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r5.anchor: المعنى خلط كل واحد منهما بالآخر فكل واحد منهما مخلوط ومخلوط به

NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r6.claim: The commentary does not separately state that they repented because their confession of sins itself indicates repentance.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p107#3/r6.anchor: ولم يذكر توبتهم لأنه ذكر اعترافهم بذنوبهم وهو دليل على التوبة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says there were ten penitents, including Abū Lubāba; a third of their wealth was taken as expiation for their sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا عشرة أنفس منهم أبو لبابة فأخذ ثلث أموالهم وكانت كفارة الذنوب التي أصابوها

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r3.claim: The sinful deed was staying behind from the campaign; the commentators who hold this account agree on that point.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r3.anchor: فكان عملهم السيء التخلف بإجماع من أهل هذه المقالة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r4.speaker: الطبري وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others identify the good deed as confession, repentance, and remorse.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r4.anchor: فقال الطبري وغيره: الاعتراف والتوبة والندم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r5.claim: Another account says their good deed was joining the Prophet, tying themselves to mosque pillars, and vowing to avoid family until God disclosed their pardon.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r5.anchor: وقيل: عملهم الصالح الذي عملوه أنهم لحقوا برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وربطوا أنفسهم بسواري المسجد

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r6.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r6.claim: A group says their good deed was taking part in earlier campaigns with the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل العمل الصالح غزوهم فيما سلف من غزو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r7.claim: Although revealed about Bedouins, the verse remains general until the Resurrection: anyone mixing good and bad deeds has grounds for hope.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r7.anchor: وهذه الآية وإن كانت نزلت في أعراب فهي عامة إلى يوم القيامة فيمن له أعمال صالحة وسيئة فهي ترجى

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r8.speaker: أبو عثمان
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r8.claim: Abū ʿUthmān calls this the Qurʾān’s most hopeful verse for the Muslim community.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r8.anchor: ذكر الطبري عن حجاج بن أبي زينب قال: سمعت أبا عثمان يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r9.claim: In the Bukhārī report from Samura ibn Jundub, the Prophet sees people partly beautiful and partly ugly; after bathing in a river they become beautiful, and he identifies them as those who mixed good and bad deeds whom God pardoned.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r9.anchor: وفي البخاري عن سمرة بن جندب قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r10.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits an Israʾ report from Abū Hurayra: Abraham identifies the blemished people as those who mixed good and bad, repented, and were forgiven; three rivers signify mercy, favor, and a pure drink.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r10.anchor: وذكر البيهقي من حديث الربيع بن أنس عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حديث الإسراء

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r1.claim: One grammatical interpretation takes the conjunction wāw as meaning bi- (with), so the phrase means mixing a good deed with a bad one.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r1.anchor: والواو في قوله: { وآخر سيئا } قيل: هي بمعنى الباء

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes wāw as maʿa (with), like the expression that water is level with the wood.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: بمعنى مع كقولك استوى الماء والخشبة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r3.claim: The Kufan grammarians reject the maʿa interpretation: wood cannot precede water, whereas the verse permits the second object to precede the first; they parse it like mixing water with milk.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102#2/r3.anchor: وأنكر ذلك الكوفيون وقالوا: لأن الخشبة لا يجوز تقديمها على الماء

QASHANI:9:100-102/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:100-102/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:100-102/r5.claim: Confession preserves the light of preparedness and pliancy, showing capacity to repent and a heart’s insight into sin; entrenched darkness would make the person see sin as good.
QASHANI:9:100-102/r5.anchor: هو إبقاء نور الاستعداد ولين الشكيمة وعدم رسوخ ملكة الذنب فيه لأنه ملك الرجوع والتوبة ودليل رؤية قبح الذنب التي لا تكون إلا بنور البصيرة وانفتاح عين القلب

QASHANI:9:100-102/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:100-102/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:100-102/r6.claim: They are at the level of the self-reproaching soul, whose connection to the heart is not yet habitual: sometimes it submits to the heart’s light and does good, and sometimes its veiling qualities prevail and it does evil.

QASHANI:9:100-102/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:100-102/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:100-102/r7.claim: If heart-lights, good deeds, and angelic thoughts prevail until obedience becomes habitual, the soul is restored and saved; if darkness and repeated sin prevail, preparedness disappears and punishment is deserved.
QASHANI:9:100-102/r7.anchor: فإن ترجحت الأنوار القلبية والأعمال الصالحة وتعاقبت عليها الخواطر الملكية

QASHANI:9:100-102/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:100-102/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:100-102/r8.claim: Which side prevails depends on companionship: providence may lead someone to righteous people and their conduct, while abandonment leads to corrupt company and loss.
QASHANI:9:100-102/r8.anchor: لا يكون إلا بالصحبة ومجالسة أصحاب كل واحد من الصنفين

QASHANI:9:102/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:102/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:102/r1.claim: God’s forgiveness covers their dark sins, and His mercy grants success in good works and accepts repentance.
QASHANI:9:102/r1.anchor: يغفر لهم السيئات المظلمة ويسترها عنهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r22.claim: Acknowledgment of wrongdoing confirms other people’s rights in court, but confession to God leads to pardon through His generosity.
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r22.anchor: الإقرار بحق الله - سبحانه - يوجب إسقاط الجرم

QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r23.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r23.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r23.claim: A poem illustrates that an apology can serve as compensation for a wrong.
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r23.anchor: وفي معناه أنشدوا : قيل لي : قد أساء فيك فلان . . . وسكوت الفتى على الضيم عار

QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r24.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r24.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r24.claim: The wording proves that a lapse does not cancel the reward of obedience: if it did, the deed could not still be called righteous.
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r24.anchor: ففي قوله : { وآخر سيئا } بعد قوله : { صالحا } دليل على أن الزلة لا تحبط ثواب الطاعة ؛ إذ لو أحبطته لم يكن العمل صالحا

QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r25.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r25.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r25.claim: The word “perhaps” means nothing is incumbent on God: He may forgive or not, and what He promises happens by His truth, not as a debt owed to anyone.
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r25.anchor: وعسى تفيد أنه لا يجب على الله شيء فقد يتوب وقد لا يتوب . ولأن قوله صدق . . فإذا أخبر أنه يجيب فإنه يفعل

QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r26.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r26.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r26.claim: Another reading takes the righteous deed to mean repentance and the bad deed to mean revoking that repentance by returning to the abandoned sin.
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r26.anchor: ويقال قوله : { خلطوا عملا صالحا } : يحتمل معناه أنهم يتوبون ؛ فالتوبة عمل صالح . وقوله : { وآخر سيئا } : يحتمل أنه نقضهم التوبة

QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r27.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r27.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r27.claim: On this reading, even if they undo their repentance by relapse, God’s gracious acceptance of them remains intact.
QUSHAYRI:v1p440/r27.anchor: فتكون الإشارة في قوله : { عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم } أنهم إن نقضوا توبتهم وعادوا إلى ما تركوه من زلتهم

STUDYQURAN:9:102/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r1.speaker: the most common account
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r1.claim: The verse concerns men who stayed behind from Tabūk, repented, tied themselves to mosque walls, and vowed to abstain from food and drink until pardoned.
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r1.anchor: According to the most common account, this verse was revealed in connection with several men who had remained behind from the Tabūk campaign

STUDYQURAN:9:102/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r2.claim: Some take the righteous deeds mixed with sins to include the men's earlier participation in battles alongside the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r2.anchor: could refer to the fact that some of these men had previously

STUDYQURAN:9:102/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r3.claim: Some understand God's expression may He relent as conveying necessity because it comes from God.
STUDYQURAN:9:102/r3.anchor: Some consider that, coming from God, it may be implies a necessity (R, Ṭ).

SULAMI:v1p284#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p284#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p284#2/r1.claim: The repentant turn from sins, confess past wrongs, regret and seek forgiveness, remember sins while forgetting their acts of obedience, and beseech God from need, hoping He opens the door of repentance to them.
SULAMI:v1p284#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : صفة النادمين والمعرضين عن الذنوب والناوين للتوبة ، وهو الاعتراف بما سبق منهم ، وكثرة الندم على ذلك والاستغفار منه

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r1.claim: Some people of Medina hardened in hypocrisy, but these others admitted their sins; their good deed was confession and repentance, and their evil deed was staying behind when the Prophet went out and abandoning jihad.

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r2.claim: Some Basran grammarians allow the omitted sense 'with another bad act,' as Arabic permits a preposition to be understood in phrases such as mixing water and milk.
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r2.anchor: فكان بعض نحويي البصرة يقول: قيل ذلك كذلك، وجائز في العربية أن يكون بآخر

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r3.claim: Other grammarians reject comparison with استوى الماء والخشبة: mixing governs both objects in either order, but that idiom cannot put the wood before the water.
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r3.anchor: وأنكر آخرون أن يكون نظير قولهم: استوى الماء والخشبة

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the sense of 'I mixed water and milk,' meaning that one mixes water with the milk.
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي أنه بمعنى قولهم: خلطت الماء واللبن

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r5.claim: Although عسى follows ordinary Arabic usage, when God says it, it is certain: the meaning is that He will forgive them.
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r5.anchor: وعسى من الله واجب، وإنما معناه: سيتوب الله عليهم، ولكنه في كلام العرب على ما وصفت

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r6.claim: God pardons and covers the sins of whoever repents, and is merciful rather than punishing them for those sins.
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r6.anchor: إن الله ذو صفح وعفو لمن تاب عن ذنوبه وساتر له عليها رحيم أن يعذبه بها

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r7.claim: One reported occasion says ten people stayed behind at Tabuk, including Abu Lubaba; seven bound themselves to mosque pillars in repentance, and after the verse was revealed the Prophet released and excused them.
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} [التوبة: 102] قال: كانوا عشرة رهط تخلفوا عن النبي

TAB-FULL:v11p650/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r8.claim: Another reported view says the group consisted of six people, one of them Abu Lubaba.
TAB-FULL:v11p650/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل كانوا ستة، أحدهم أبو لبابة

TAB-FULL:v11p653/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p653/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p653/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a six-person account: Abu Lubaba and five others stayed behind at Tabuk; Abu Lubaba and two companions bound themselves, three did not, and the Prophet released and excused the repentant men after revelation.
TAB-FULL:v11p653/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله} [التوبة: 102]

TAB-FULL:v11p653/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p653/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p653/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the people who tied themselves to the pillars as eight, including Kurdam, Mirdas, and Abu Lubaba.
TAB-FULL:v11p653/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم إن الله غفور رحيم} [التوبة: 102]

TAB-FULL:v11p654/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r1.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r1.claim: Sa'id names Hilal, Abu Lubaba, Kurdam, Mirdas, and Abu Qays among those who tied themselves to the pillars.
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r1.anchor: عن جعفر، عن سعيد، قال: " الذين ربطوا أنفسهم بالسواري: هلال، وأبو لبابة، وكردم، ومرداس، وأبو قيس

TAB-FULL:v11p654/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r2.claim: Qatada says seven stayed behind at Tabuk; four who mixed good and bad deeds were Jad ibn Qays, Abu Lubaba, Hiram, and Aws, all Ansar, and they are those addressed in 9:103.
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم} [التوبة: 102] ذكر لنا أنهم كانوا سبعة رهط

TAB-FULL:v11p654/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r3.claim: In another report, Qatada says the group numbered seven, including Abu Lubaba, and explicitly rejects the claim that there were only three.
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r3.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم} [التوبة: 102] قال: هم سبعة، منهم أبو لبابة

TAB-FULL:v11p654/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak recounts that Abu Lubaba and companions regretted staying in comfort while the Prophet fought, tied themselves up, and were released and excused after the revelation.
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r4.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} [التوبة: 102] نزلت في أبي لبابة وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v11p654/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r5.claim: Another view says the verse concerns Abu Lubaba alone and the sin he admitted from his dealings with Banu Qurayza.
TAB-FULL:v11p654/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عني بهذه الآية أبو لبابة خاصة وذنبه الذي اعترف به فتيب عليه منه ما كان من أمره في بني قريظة

TAB-FULL:v11p657/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r1.claim: Mujahid connects the verse to Abu Lubaba's warning to Banu Qurayza that Muhammad would slaughter them if they accepted God's judgment; Abu Lubaba indicated his throat.
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم} [التوبة: 102] قال: نزلت في أبي لبابة قال لبني قريظة ما قال

TAB-FULL:v11p657/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r2.claim: Mujahid also says Abu Lubaba tied himself to a pillar, vowing not to release himself until God and His Messenger did so; the Prophet freed him, and the verse was revealed about him.
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، " ربط أبو لبابة نفسه إلى سارية، فقال: لا أحل نفسي حتى يحلني الله ورسوله

TAB-FULL:v11p657/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r3.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r3.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that Abu Lubaba stayed behind at Tabuk, fasted while bound for seven days until unconscious, then insisted the Prophet free him; he pledged his property, but the Prophet limited the donation to one third.
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r3.anchor: قال الزهري: " كان أبو لبابة ممن تخلف عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك، فربط نفسه بسارية

TAB-FULL:v11p657/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation says the verse refers to Bedouins.
TAB-FULL:v11p657/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: عنى بهذه الآية الأعراب

TAB-FULL:v11p658/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the confessors as Bedouins.
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} [التوبة: 102] قال: فقال إنهم من الأعراب "

TAB-FULL:v11p658/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r2.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says no Qurʾānic passage gives him greater hope for this community than this verse through “God is forgiving, merciful.”
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا عثمان، يقول: " ما في القرآن أرجى عندي لهذه الأمة من قوله: {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم}

TAB-FULL:v11p658/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that this refers to a group who admitted their error in staying behind the Prophet and missing the Tabūk expedition against the Romans; Abū Lubāba was among them. The plural excludes the single person bound to a pillar at Qurayẓa, and the exegetes agree Abū Lubāba belonged to the group.
TAB-FULL:v11p658/r3.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى هذه الأقوال بالصواب في ذلك قول من قال: نزلت هذه الآية في المعترفين

TABRISI:9:101-102/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102/r6.claim: Ākharūn is coordinated with the earlier mention of Bedouin hypocrites; ākarūn murjawna may be coordinated there too, or minhum supplied.

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r1.claim: These other people may be from Medina or the Bedouins; they are not a reference back to the hypocrites.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r1.anchor: يعني من أهل المدينة أو من الأعراب آخرون أقروا بذنوبهم وليس براجع إلى المنافقين

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r2.claim: Iʿtirāf is acknowledging something with knowledge of it.

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r3.claim: They performed both good, commendable acts and evil, reprehensible ones.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r3.anchor: يعني أنهم يفعلون أفعالا جميلة ويفعلون أفعالا سيئة قبيحة

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r4.claim: The syntax implies a second noun: they mixed a good deed with another, bad deed.

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r5.claim: The commentators say God's ʿasā is sure; its wording keeps sinners between hope and fear and discourages reliance on pardon instead of repenting.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: عسى من الله واجبه وإنما قال عسى حتى يكونوا بين طمع وإشفاق

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r6.claim: The verse disproves the doctrine that one deed cancels another: if so, the two deeds could not be mixed, making the wording meaningless.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r6.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على بطلان القول بالإحباط لأنه لو صح الإحباط لكان أحد العملين

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r7.speaker: بعض التابعين
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r7.claim: Some Successors call this the Qurʾān's most hopeful verse for this community.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعض التابعين ما في القرآن آية أرجى لهذه الأمة من هذه الآية

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r8.claim: Mixing can mean joining without blending, as when one says that dirhams and dinars are mixed.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r8.anchor: وقد يستعمل لفظ الخلط في الجمع من غير امتزاج يقال خلط الدراهم والدنانير

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r9.claim: Another explanation compares the phrase to water being level with a plank, meaning alongside it.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: إنه يجري مجرى قولهم استوى الماء والخشبة أي مع الخشبة

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r10.claim: A reported form uses lightening for the good deed and gemination for the evil deed.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن خلط بالتخفيف في الخير وخلط بالتشديد في الشر

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r11.claim: God's forgiveness and mercy explain His acceptance of sinners' repentance.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r11.anchor: هذا تعليل لقبول التوبة من العصاة أي لأنه غفور رحيم

TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r12.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r12.claim: Abū Ḥamza reports that three Anṣār who stayed behind at Tabūk bound themselves to mosque pillars, were released when the repentance verse came, and offered their wealth for charity; the command to take charity came in 9:103.
TABRISI:9:101-102#2/r12.anchor:
قال أبو حمزة الثمالي:
" بلغنا أنهم ثلاثة نفر من الأنصار أبو لبابة بن عبد المنذر

TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r1.claim: One account says the penitents numbered ten, including Abū Lubāba, transmitted by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās.
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنهم كانوا عشرة رهط منهم أبو لبابة عن علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، زيد بن أسلم
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam say there were eight, including Abū Lubāba, Hilāl, Kardam, and Abū Qays.
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: كانوا ثمانية منهم أبو لبابة وهلال وكردم وأبو قيس عن سعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r3.claim: Qatāda says the group numbered seven; another account says five.
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: كانوا سبعة عن قتادة. وقيل: كانوا خمسة

TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir says the verse concerned Abū Lubāba alone; the occasion was his warning to Banū Qurayẓa that surrendering to their judge meant slaughter, also attributed to Mujāhid.
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع: أنها نزلت في أبي لبابة ولم يذكر غيره معه

TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r5.speaker: الزهري
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r5.claim: Another account makes Abū Lubāba's repentance the occasion: after staying behind at Tabūk, he tied himself to a pillar, as related through al-Zuhrī.
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r5.anchor: وقيل: نزلت فيه خاصة حين تأخر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك

TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r6.speaker: أبو لبابة
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r6.claim: Abū Lubāba offered to leave the home where he sinned and give all his wealth; the Prophet said one third would suffice.
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r6.anchor:
ثم قال أبو لبابة:
" يا رسول الله إن من توبتي أن أهجر دار قومي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وآخرون} أي ومن أهل المدينة آخرون {اعترفوا بذنوبهم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r2.speaker: أصحاب العربية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r2.claim: Iʿtirāf is admission of a matter with knowledge; the passage also associates confessing with humility, submission, and acceptance of abasement.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r3.claim: The verse concerns believers who stayed behind from Tabuk, regretted it, and bound themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet released them; after returning, he waited for God's command, then released and excused them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p30#2/r3.anchor: وقال أهل التفسير: (نزلت في قوم من المؤمنين، كانوا تخلفوا عن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- عن (¬3) غزوة تبوك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r1.claim: The good deed is a sincere intention and disavowal of hypocrisy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد نية صادقة وبراءة من النفاق)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the sin as staying behind from the campaign, the good deed as repentance, and the evil deed as failing to join the campaign.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: {اعترفوا بذنوبهم} يعني التخلف عن الغزو، و {خلطوا عملا صالحا} يعني التوبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the good deed as their earlier jihad with the Prophet and the evil deed as staying behind from Tabuk.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: (العمل الصالح: خروجهم إلى الجهاد مع النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قبل هذا، والسيء: تخلفهم عن تبوك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ transmits both interpretations: repentance paired with failure to campaign, and earlier jihad paired with staying behind at Tabuk.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r5.claim: Arabic allows “I mixed water with milk” with bāʾ and “I mixed water and milk” with wāw.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r5.anchor: والعرب تقول: خلطت الماء باللبن، وخلطت الماء واللبن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r6.claim: The wāw is better than bāʾ because the verse means combining two deeds, not literally mixing them as liquids.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p31/r6.anchor: والواو في الآية أحسن من الباء؛ لأنه أريد معنى الجمع لا حقيقة الخلط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
