WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r1.claim: When God says “perhaps,” it is certain that He will act; they cite God's promise of victory, which came to pass, and say He likewise accepted these people's repentance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: ((عسى) من الله واجب) (¬4). لأنه قال: {فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح} [المائدة: 52] ففعل ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r2.claim: The wording keeps people between hope and apprehension, discouraging complacency and neglect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p32/r2.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (لفظ (عسى) هاهنا بيان عن أنه ينبغي أن يكونوا على الطمع والإشفاق؛ لأنه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r6.claim: They confessed to staying behind from the expedition; their good deed was earlier jihad with the Prophet and their bad deed missing this campaign.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r6.anchor: { وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم } في التخلف عن الغزو { خلصوا عملا صالحا } وهو جهادهم مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل هذا { وآخر سيئا } تقاعدهم عن هذه الغزوة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r7.claim: “Perhaps God will repent toward them” is an assured promise; God then forgave them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r7.anchor: { عسى الله } واجب من الله { أن يتوب عليهم إن الله غفور رحيم } ثم تاب على هؤلاء وعذرهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r8.claim: They offered the property that kept them back as charity and sought purification and forgiveness; the Prophet said he was not ordered to take it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:100-102/r8.anchor: فقالوا: يا رسول الله، هذه أموالنا التي خلفتنا عنك فخذها منا صدقة وطهرنا، واستغفر لنا، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما أمرت أن آخذ من أموالكم شيئا.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r1.claim: Some sincere believers waver between right and wrong and mix conduct befitting a believer with conduct that is not.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r1.anchor: Esasen samimi bir imana sahip olmakla beraber, zaman zaman hakla bâtıl arasında med cezirler yaşayan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r2.claim: On honest self-examination they recognize their inconsistency, repent, admit their sins, and do not try to excuse themselves like those who only pretend to believe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r2.anchor: gerçek mânada inanmadığı halde inanmış gibi görünenlerin girdiği yola girmeyip kendilerini mâzur göstermeye çalışmazlar, günahlarını itiraf ederler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r3.claim: Although translated “perhaps,” when asa is used of God it indicates that the promised matter will happen, since God's generosity has no limit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r3.anchor: “Umulur ki” şeklinde tercüme edilen “asâ” yardımcı fiilinin Cenâb-ı Allah hakkında kullanılması, belirtilen hususun gerçekleşeceği anlamındadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r4.speaker: rivayetler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r4.claim: Reports differ in details but agree that the verse concerns people who could have joined Tabuk, stayed behind, then sincerely regretted it and confessed without inventing excuses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r4.anchor: Âyetin inmesine vesile olan olayla ilgili rivayetlerin ayrıntılarında farklılıklar bulunmakla beraber bunlar, âyette, durumları müsait olduğu halde Tebük Seferi’ne katılmaktan kaçınıp

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r5.claim: After hearing verses about those who stayed behind, the repentant men felt such remorse that they tied themselves to the mosque pillars and vowed not to leave until the Prophet released them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r5.anchor: Bu kişiler sefere çıkmaktan geri kalanlarla ilgili âyetleri duyunca öylesine bir vicdan azabı ve pişmanlık hissetmişlerdi ki, kendilerini Mescid-i Nebevî’nin direklerine bağlamışlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r6.claim: When the Prophet returned, he first went to the mosque; after hearing why they were bound, he vowed to await revelation before freeing or pardoning them, then the verse came and he released and accepted their apology.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:102/r6.anchor: Resûlullah vahiy gelinceye kadar kendisinin de onları çözmeyeceğine ve özürlerini kabul etmeyeceğine yemin etti. Bunun üzerine bu âyet nâzil oldu

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p124/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p124/r1.speaker: أم سلمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p124/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that she heard the Prophet say at dawn that God had accepted Abū Lubāba's repentance; she told him, and the Prophet released him after morning prayer. The chain contains al-Wāqidī.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p124/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه بسند فيه الواقدي عن أم سلمة قالت إن توبة أبي لبابة نزلت في بيتي فسمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يضحك في السحر

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r1.claim: These are another group of sinful Bedouins, unlike the hypocrites: they acknowledged their sins and mixed good deeds with bad, so God's turning to them remains possible.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r1.anchor: أي ومن الأعراب جماعة آخرون مذنبون لا ينافقون مثل غيرهم بل اعترفوا بذنوبهم لهم عمل صالح

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r2.claim: The wording instills hope so their souls remain between fear and hope rather than falling into despair.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r2.anchor: وفي قوله { عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم } إيجاد الرجاء في نفوسهم

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r3.claim: Calling God forgiving and merciful gives greater weight to hope.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r3.anchor: وفي قوله { إن الله غفور رحيم } ترجيح جانب الرجاء

TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r5.claim: A report from Imam al-Bāqir identifies them as believers who commit sins that believers disapprove of and dislike, for whom God's turning remains possible.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو جعفر عليه السلام { الذين خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا } فأولئك قوم مؤمنون يحدثون

TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r6.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī's report from Zurāra gives the same explanation but has 'sinners' in place of 'believers'.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r6.anchor: ورواه العياشي عن زرارة عنه عليه السلام إلا أن فيه { مذنبون } { مكان مؤمنون }

TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r7.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r7.claim: Abū Ḥamza al-Thumālī says he was told that three Anṣār—Abū Kināna, Thaʿlaba b. Wadīʿa and Aws b. Ḥidhām—stayed behind at Tabūk, bound themselves to mosque pillars in remorse, and awaited the Prophet's return and release.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#3/r7.anchor: قال أبو حمزة الثمالي بلغنا أنهم ثلاثة نفر من الأنصار أبو كنانة بن عبد المنذر وثعلبة بن وديعة

TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r1.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r1.claim: In Abū Ḥamza's account, the Prophet would not release the three men first without a divine instruction; after this verse was revealed, he freed them, and they offered the wealth that had kept them back as charity, but he said he had not been ordered to take it.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r1.anchor: وأنا أقسم لا أكون أول من حلهم إلا أن أومر فيهم بأمر

THALABI:v5p88/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p88/r1.claim: “Others” refers to some people of Medina or some Bedouins, not to the previously mentioned hypocrites.
THALABI:v5p88/r1.anchor: وآخرون يعني ومن أهل المدينة آخرون أو من الأعراب وليس براجع إلى المنافقين

THALABI:v5p88/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p88/r2.claim: They admitted their guilt to the Prophet and to their Lord.

THALABI:v5p88/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p88/r3.claim: Their good deed is confession and repentance; the bad deed is another sinful act, namely staying behind from the Messenger and leaving jihad.
THALABI:v5p88/r3.anchor: وهو إقرارهم وتوبتهم وآخر سيئا أي بعمل سيئ

THALABI:v5p88/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p88/r4.claim: The conjunction wāw stands in place of bi, as in expressions meaning that water was mixed with impurity or milk with water.
THALABI:v5p88/r4.anchor: وضع الواو وموضع الياء فكما يقال: استوى الماء والخبث

THALABI:v5p88/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p88/r5.claim: Their hoped-for repentance concerns those who confessed their sins; when God uses ʿasā or laʿalla, the promised outcome is certain.
THALABI:v5p88/r5.anchor: عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم وعسى ولعل من الله واجب وهما حرف ترج

THALABI:v5p88/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p88/r6.claim: After missing the Tabūk expedition, a group regretted staying home and chained themselves to mosque pillars, vowing to remain until the Messenger released or punished them. He initially refused; after revelation he freed and excused them, and they offered their wealth as expiation, prompting the order to take alms.
THALABI:v5p88/r6.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في قوم كانوا تخلفوا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك ثم ندموا عليه

THALABI:v5p88/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p88/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's report that there were ten men, including Abū Lubāba.
THALABI:v5p88/r7.anchor: علي بن ابي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: كانوا عشرة رهط منهم أبو لبابة

THALABI:v5p88/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وزيد بن أسلم أبو منية
THALABI:v5p88/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam Abū Munya name Hilāl, Abū Lubāba, Kardam, Mirdās, and Abū Qays among them.
THALABI:v5p88/r8.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وزيد بن أسلم أبو [منية] : منهم هلال وأبو لبابة وكردم ومرداس وأبو قيس

THALABI:v5p88/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p88/r9.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
THALABI:v5p88/r9.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say there were seven, including Jad ibn Qays, Abū Lubāba, Juthām, and Aws, all from the Anṣār.
THALABI:v5p88/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة والضحاك: كانوا سبعة منهم جد بن قيس وأبو لبابة وجذام وأوس

THALABI:v5p89/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r1.speaker: عطية
THALABI:v5p89/r1.claim: ʿAṭiyya transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's view that there were five men, one of them Abū Lubāba.
THALABI:v5p89/r1.anchor: وقال عطية عن ابن عباس: كانوا خمسة أحدهم أبو لبابة

THALABI:v5p89/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p89/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the verse concerns Abū Lubāba's signal to Qurayẓa that surrendering to the Prophet's judgment meant execution; he regretted the act, repented, and confessed.
THALABI:v5p89/r2.anchor: فقال مجاهد: نزلت هذه الآية في أبي لبابة

THALABI:v5p89/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r3.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v5p89/r3.claim: Al-Zuhrī says Abū Lubāba tied himself to a pillar after missing Tabūk and vowed not to eat or drink until he died or God accepted his repentance. After seven days he fainted; the verse came, and the Prophet released him. Abū Lubāba then vowed all his wealth as charity, but the Prophet said a third sufficed.
THALABI:v5p89/r3.anchor: قال الزهري: نزلت في تخلفه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك فربط نفسه بسارية

THALABI:v5p89/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
THALABI:v5p89/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say these penitents were different from the three who remained behind.
THALABI:v5p89/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: هؤلاء سوى الثلاثة الذين تخلفوا

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r5.claim: Unlike the other absentees, this group did not invent excuses: they admitted the wrong of missing the expedition without excuse, regretted it, and confessed honestly.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r5.anchor: öbürleri gibi yalandan mazeretlerle i‘tizâra kalkışmadılar

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r6.claim: Their good and bad deeds were mixed: they had gone on some expeditions and missed others, sinned, then regretted and acknowledged their sins.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r6.anchor: fena amel de yaptılar iyi[^2] de; meselâ gazâya gittikleri de oldu gitmedikleri de.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r7.claim: Some of those who had stayed behind tied themselves to the mosque pillars and swore they would not untie themselves until the Prophet did; he also waited for a command, and this verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r7.anchor: mütehallifler hakkında nâzil olan âyetleri işittiklerinde kendilerini Mescid-i Saâdet’in üstüvânelerine bağlamışlardı.

BURHAN:v3p152/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p152/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p152/r9.claim: The preposition and complement are omitted: they mingled a good deed with a bad one, and another bad deed with a good one.

ITQAN:v3p165/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p165/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p165/r2.claim: The compact wording implies that they mixed a good deed with a bad one, and another bad deed with a good one.
ITQAN:v3p165/r2.anchor: أي عملا صالحا بسيئ وآخر سيئا صالح

AKHFASH:v1p364/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p364/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p364/r2.claim: The construction can omit bi- before the second object, as in khalatū bi-ākhar, like istawā al-māʾ wa-l-khashabata meaning with the timber.
AKHFASH:v1p364/r2.anchor: فيجوز في العربية ان تكون "بآخر" كما تقول: "استوى الماء والخشبة"

FARRA:v1p450/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p450/r3.speaker: يقال
FARRA:v1p450/r3.claim: One explanation says their good deed was going out to Badr and witnessing it.

FARRA:v1p450/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p450/r4.speaker: يقال
FARRA:v1p450/r4.claim: Another explanation takes the good deed as their repentance for staying behind from the Tabuk expedition.
FARRA:v1p450/r4.anchor: ويقال: العمل الصالح توبتهم من تخلفهم عن غزوة تبوك.

FARRA:v1p450/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p450/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p450/r5.claim: Their bad deed was remaining behind at Tabuk; God's عسى is a sure promise, God willing.
FARRA:v1p450/r5.anchor: وآخر سيئا: تخلفهم يوم تبوك عسى الله عسى من الله واجب إن شاء الله.

FARRA:v1p506/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p506/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p506/r1.claim: The verse concerning those who mixed righteous and bad deeds was revealed about people who attended Badr and then stayed behind from Tabuk.
FARRA:v1p506/r1.anchor: «خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا» نزلت فيمن شهد بدرا، وتخلف عن تبوك

ASAD-NOTES:9:102/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102/r1.claim: The people have recognized their sin after mixing righteous acts with evil, and God may still accept their repentance.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102/r1.anchor: have become conscious of their sinning after having done righteous deeds side by side with evil ones; [136] [and] it may well be that God will accept their repentance

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r1.claim: These others are from the people of Medina or the Bedouins, and are not the hypocrites.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وآخرون} أي: ومن أهل المدينة، أو: من الأعراب آخرون، ولا يرجع هذا إلى المنافقين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r2.anchor: ولا يرجع هذا إلى المنافقين، {اعترفوا} أقروا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r3.claim: The good deed is their acknowledgment and repentance; the bad deed is another bad act, with the conjunction و used in the sense of ب, like mixing water with milk.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r3.anchor: وآخر سيئا} أي: بعمل آخر سيئ، وضع الواو موضع الباء، كما يقال: خلطت الماء واللبن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r4.claim: The good deed is their remorse and tying themselves to the mosque pillars; another reported explanation counts their campaigns with the Prophet as good deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r4.anchor: والعمل الصالح: هو ندامتهم وربطهم أنفسهم بالسواري وقيل: غزواتهم مع النبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.claim: The verse concerns people who stayed behind from the Tabūk expedition, repented, and bound themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet would release and excuse them; God revealed the verse and he released them. They offered their wealth for charity, but he said he had not been commanded to take it, and 9:103 then came down.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.anchor: فلما رجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بهم فرآهم فقال: من هؤلاء؟ فقالوا: هؤلاء الذين تخلفوا عنك فعاهدوا الله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r1.claim: This is the gentle, pure counterpart to the preceding harsh group: the party whose repentance has been completed and whom God regards with mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر هذا القسم المارد الجافي , ثنى بمقابلة اللين الصافي , وهي الفرقة التي نجز المتاب عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r2.claim: They deliberately named their sins in repentance, with regret, cessation, and resolve, rather than resorting to false excuses; they are those who stayed behind.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r2.anchor: { اعترفوا بذنوبهم } أي كلفوا أنفسهم ذكرها توبة منهم ندما وإقلاعا وعزما ولم يفزعوا إلى المعاذير الكاذبة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r3.claim: The conjunction in 'another' evokes intermixture on both sides, an elegant iḥtibāk: they mixed good with evil and evil with good, suggesting neither was predominant.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r3.anchor: فالإتيان بالواو في { آخر } يفهم أن المعنى : { خلطوا عملا صالحا } بسيئ { وآخر سيئا } بصالح

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r4.claim: Biqāʿī calls this a subtle instance of iḥtibāk and says the wording suggests the two kinds of deed are balanced, with neither taking priority as the basis.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r4.anchor: فهو من ألطف شاهد لنوع الاحتباك , ولعل التعبير بما أفهم ذلك إشارة إلى تساوي العلمين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r5.claim: Samura reports in Bukhari's tafsir that the Prophet saw half-beautiful, half-ugly men become wholly beautiful after entering a river; they were people who mixed good and evil, whom God pardoned.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r5.anchor: وقد فسرها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك في أناس رآهم في المنام شطر منهم حسن

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r6.claim: God's 'perhaps' assures hope of their repentance, although no one is entitled to anything from Him and every kindness is grace.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r6.anchor: فإن { عسى } منه سبحانه وتعالى واجبه لأن هذا دأب الملوك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r7.claim: Their restored status is like that of ordinary believers, who are not infallible and, despite lapses, expect mercy when they return to vigilance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r7.anchor: فكما ان أولئك معدودون في حزب الله مع هذا التقصير المرجو له العفو فكذلك هؤلاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r8.claim: God is always characterized by accepting the one who turns back and, through favor and generosity, replacing an evil deed with a good one.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r8.anchor: { إن الله } أي ذا الجلال والإكرام { غفور رحيم * } أي لم يزل موصوفا بقبول المعرض إذا أقبل

DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.claim: An unattributed report fragment repeats that some people are present and urges asking God for well-being; Umar then questions an allied man about an unnamed Prophetic sermon and rebukes him.
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.anchor: ثم قال: إن منكم وإن منكم وإن منكم فسلوا الله العافية فلقي عمر رضي الله عنه رجلا كان بينه وبينه إخاء

DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that ten men delayed from Tabūk; seven tied themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet released and pardoned them after God revealed 9:102. They offered their wealth for charity and forgiveness; after he said he was not commanded to take it, 9:103 directed him to take alms, purify them, and pray for them. Three others were deferred a year until the revelation of 9:117 and the passage about the three.
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} قال كانوا عشرة رهط تخلفوا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك فلما حضر رجوع رسول الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r1.claim: The verse concerns another group among these factions who acknowledged their sins and mixed good deeds with bad ones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r1.anchor: المعنى ومن هذه الطوائف آخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عثمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿUthmān say the verse concerns Bedouins and broadly applies until the Resurrection to anyone combining good and bad deeds, making it a verse of hope.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس فيما روي عنه وأبو عثمان: هي في الأعراب وهي عامة في الأمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r3.claim: Abū ʿUthmān calls this one of the Quran’s most hopeful verses for the community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r3.anchor: أسند الطبري هذا عن حجاج بن أبي زينب قال سمعت أبا عثمان يقول: ما في القرآن آية أرجى عندي لهذه الأمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r4.claim: Qatāda says the verse was revealed specifically about Abū Lubāba’s affair with Banū Qurayẓa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة بل نزلت هذه الآية في أبي لبابة الأنصاري خاصة في شأنه مع بني قريظة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r5.claim: In the Abū Lubāba account, he advised Banū Qurayẓa to surrender to God and the Messenger’s judgment, then gestured to his throat to signal that they would be killed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r5.anchor: فأشار هو لهم إلى حلقه يريد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يذبحهم إن نزلوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r6.claim: After his gesture was exposed, Abū Lubāba repented, bound himself to a mosque pillar, and vowed to fast until God pardoned him or he died; God pardoned him and the Prophet released him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r6.anchor: فلما افتضح تاب وندم وربط نفسه في سارية من سواري المسجد، وأقسم أن لا يطعم ولا يشرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī attributes the Abū Lubāba report to Mujāhid; Ibn Isḥāq’s version in the biography is fuller and more exact.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r7.anchor: وذكر هذا الطبري عن مجاهد، وذكره ابن إسحاق في كتاب السير أوعب وأتقن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r8.speaker: فرقة عظيمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r8.claim: A large group says the verse concerns those who stayed behind from the Tabūk expedition; they agree that staying behind was the bad deed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة عظيمة: بل نزلت هذه الآية في شأن المتخلفين عن غزوة تبوك، فكان عملهم السيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r9.speaker: الطبري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others identify the good deed of the Tabūk stay-behind group as confession, repentance, and remorse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r9.anchor: واختلفوا في «الصالح» فقال الطبري وغيره الاعتراف والتوبة والندم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r10.claim: Another group identifies the good deed as their participation in earlier campaigns with the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r10.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل «الصالح» غزوهم فيما سلف من غزو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the group numbered ten: seven bound themselves, while the three later mentioned as left behind did not bind themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r11.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كانوا عشرة رهط ربط منهم أنفسهم سبعة، وبقي الثلاثة الذين خلفوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r12.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r12.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam counts eight, including Kardam, Mirdās, Abū Qays, and Abū Lubāba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r12.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم كانوا ثمانية منهم كردم ومرداس وأبو قيس وأبو لبابة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r13.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r13.claim: Qatāda counts seven people in the group.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة: كانوا سبعة، وقال ابن عباس أيضا وفرقة: كانوا خمسة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وفرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and another group count five; all the reported counts include Abū Lubāba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وفرقة: كانوا خمسة، وكلهم قال كان فيهم أبو لبابة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r15.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r15.claim: Qatāda includes al-Jadd ibn Qays among them, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya regards that as mistaken because al-Jadd’s departure was not a repentance case.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r15.anchor: وذكر قتادة فيهم الجد بن قيس وهو فيما أعلم وهم لأن الجد لم يكن نزوله توبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r16.claim: Ākhar is equivalent to bi-ākhar; the two expressions are close in meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r16.anchor: وأما قوله وآخر فهو بمعنى بآخر وهما متقاربان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77/r17.claim: When God uses ʿasā for a promise, its fulfillment is certain.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.claim: When the Prophet saw the people bound in the mosque, he was told they had repented and would not untie themselves until he released and excused them; he refused unless God commanded it, since they had missed the expedition and jihad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r1.anchor: وروي في خبر الذين ربطوا أنفسهم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل المسجد فرآهم

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r9.claim: Iʿtirāf is acknowledgment based on knowledge, while iqrār derives from a thing being fixed and established.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r9.anchor: الاعتراف: الإقرار بالشيء عن معرفة؛ لأن الإقرار من قر الشيء إذا ثبت،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r10.claim: The verb iʿtarafa can also mean asking people for information in order to learn it; a cited poetic line illustrates this use, and the root is knowledge, as in ʿarafa and al-Aʿrāf.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r10.anchor: واعترف الرجل القوم: إذا سألهم عن خبر ليعرفه، ومنه قول الشاعر: أسائلة عميرة عن أبيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r1.claim: They did not make false excuses for staying behind but admitted their wrongdoing with regret; the three named are Abū Lubāba Marwān b. ʿAbd al-Mundhir, Aws b. Thaʿlaba, and Wadīʿa b. Ḥizām.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r1.anchor: أي لم يعتذروا من تخلفهم بالمعاذير الكاذبة كغيرهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r2.claim: An alternative report says ten men were involved and seven tied themselves to mosque pillars, believing they were doomed; they vowed to remain bound until the Prophet released them, and he waited for revelation before freeing and excusing them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r2.anchor: وقيل : ( 488 ) كانوا عشرة ، فسبعة منهم أوثقوا أنفسهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r3.claim: After release, the men offered the wealth that had kept them back as charity for purification; the Prophet said he had not been ordered to take it, then the instruction to take charity was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r3.anchor: فقالوا : يا رسول الله ، هذه أموالنا التي خلفتنا عنك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r4.claim: The good deed means going out for jihad and the other deed means staying behind.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r5.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī instead take the good deed as repentance and the bad deed as sin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r5.anchor: عن الحسن وعن الكلبي : التوبة والإثم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r6.claim: Each deed is both mixed with and mixed into its counterpart, like saying ‘I mixed water and milk’; this differs from ‘I mixed water with milk,’ where only water is the mixed item.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r6.anchor: كل واحد منهما مخلوط ومخلوط به ؛ لأن المعنى خلط كل واحد منهما الآخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r7.claim: The coordinated construction can also be understood by analogy with ‘I sold a sheep, a sheep and a dirham,’ meaning a sheep for a dirham.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من قولهم : بعت الشاة شاة ودرهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r8.claim: Their repentance need not be separately stated: admitting their sins itself indicates repentance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p291/r8.anchor: إذا ذكر اعترافهم بذنوبهم ، وهو دليل على التوبة

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r1.claim: Their good deed was campaigning with the Prophet before Tabuk; their bad deed was staying behind from the Tabuk campaign without permission.
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r1.anchor: يعني غزاة قبل غزاة تبوك مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r2.claim: The occasion involved three Ansar: Abu Lubaba, named Marwan b. Abd al-Mundhir, Aws b. Hizam, and Wadi'a b. Thalaba, who heard the Prophet was returning from Tabuk and tied themselves to mosque pillars in remorse.
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r2.anchor: نزلت في أبي لبابة، اسمه مروان بن عبد المنذر

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r3.claim: They vowed not to release themselves until the Prophet released them; when told who they were, he vowed not to release them until commanded and not to excuse them until God did.
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r3.anchor: وأقسموا ألا يحلو أنفسهم حتى يحلهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r4.claim: Muqatil says that when God says perhaps, it is a certain promise; after this verse came down, the Prophet released them and they returned home.
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل: العسى من الله واجب

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r1.claim: Those who confessed their sins may have been hypocrites who were not entrenched in hypocrisy, or they may have been believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r1.anchor: فالصنف الأول يحتمل أنهم كانوا منافقين وما مردوا على النفاق، ويحتمل أنهم كانوا مؤمنين،

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the passage concerns ten men who stayed behind from Tabuk; seven bound themselves to pillars in the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في عشرة تخلفوا عن غزوة تبوك فأوثق سبعة منهم أنفسهم في سواري المسجد.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the group numbered eight.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r4.anchor: وقال زيد بن اسلم: كانوا ثمانية.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r5.claim: Another report gives the group’s number as six.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r6.claim: Another report gives the group’s number as five.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r9.speaker: أشهب عن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r9.claim: Ashhab reports from Malik that the deferred group was Abu Lubaba and his companions; Abu Lubaba offered to stay near the Prophet and relinquish his property.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r9.anchor: وقال أشهب عن مالك: نزلت «وآخرون» في شأن أبي لبابة وأصحابه.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.claim: The majority say the passage concerns Tabuk stay-behinds who bound themselves like Abu Lubaba, vowing not to free themselves until the Prophet released and forgave them; after the verse was revealed, he released them and they offered their wealth as charity for purification and forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.anchor: والجمهور أن الآية نزلت في شأن المتخلفين عن غزوة تبوك، وكانوا ربطوا أنفسهم كما فعل أبو لبابة

RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r1.claim: Two views identify the people who confessed: repentant hypocrites, or Muslims who missed Tabūk through laziness rather than unbelief or hypocrisy, then regretted and repented.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r1.anchor: قوله : { وءاخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم } فيه قولان : الأول

RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r2.speaker: قائلون بالقول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r2.claim: Those favoring the first view cite the conjunction with the nearby mention of hypocritical Bedouins: the first group persisted in hypocrisy, while this group was enabled to repent.

RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r3.claim: A report names three men, while another says ten, seven of whom bound themselves in the mosque. The Prophet initially refused to release them without revelation, then freed and excused them; their request that he take their wealth preceded 9:103.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r3.anchor: روي أنهم كانوا ثلاثة : أبو لبابة مروان بن عبد المنذر ، وأوس بن ثعلبة ، ووديعة بن حزام ، وقيل : كانوا عشرة

RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r4.claim: Linguistically, confession is acknowledging something with knowledge; its nuance is that they did not invent excuses but admitted wrongdoing, regretted it, and blamed themselves for staying behind.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139/r4.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : الاعتراف عبارة عن الإقرار بالشيء عن معرفة ، ومعناه أنهم أقروا بذنبهم

RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r1.claim: Confession alone is not repentance; repentance combines regret for the past and resolve to stop in future, with regret because God prohibited the act.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r1.anchor: قلنا : مجرد الاعتراف بالذنب لا يكون توبة ، فأما إذا اقترن به الندم على الماضي ، والعزم على تركه في المستقبل

RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r2.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r2.claim: Razi says the commentators take God’s use of ʿasā as indicating that their repentance will certainly be accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r2.anchor: والمفسرون قالوا : إن عسى من الله يدل على الوجوب

RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r3.speaker: الأول
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r3.claim: One interpretation makes the good deed their confession, regret, and repentance, and the bad deed their failure to join the expedition.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r3.anchor: الأول : العمل الصالح هو الاعتراف بالذنب والندامة عليه والتوبة منه ، والسيء هو التخلف عن الغزو

RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r4.speaker: الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r4.claim: A second interpretation takes their good deeds as joining the Messenger on other campaigns and the bad deed as missing Tabūk.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r4.anchor: العمل الصالح خروجهم مع الرسول إلى سائر الغزوات والسيء هو تخلفهم عن غزوة تبوك

RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r5.speaker: الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r5.claim: A third view says the verse concerns Muslims, and the good deed is the good works they had performed.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r5.anchor: أن هذه الآية نزلت في حق المسلمين كان العمل الصالح إقدامهم على أعمال البر

RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r6.claim: Here mixing means simple combination, not intermixture that changes each item’s original quality, as in mixing water and milk.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r6.anchor: واللائق بهذا الموضع هو الجمع المطلق

RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r7.claim: Razi uses the wording to reject cancellation of deeds: obedience retains its praise and reward, sin its blame and punishment; because both are described as mixed, both must remain present, since an attribute cannot exist without its subject.
RAZI-FULL:v16p139#2/r7.anchor: فدل على بقاء العملين حال الاختلاط

RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r1.claim: The commentators say divine ʿasā means certainty, citing 5:52 where the promised victory occurred; human speech conventions let a great ruler use ʿasā to signal that his acts are favor, not an obligation, while still guaranteeing the answer.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون : كلمة عسى من الله واجب ، والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : { فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح } ( المائدة : 52 )

RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r2.claim: Another answer is that ʿasā keeps the person morally responsible in hope and apprehension, discouraging denial and neglect.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r2.anchor: المقصود منه بيان أنه يجب أن يكون المكلف على الطمع والإشفاق لأنه أبعد من الإنكار والإهمال

RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r3.claim: Razi’s school reads this as repentance being created by God: regret is not chosen by the servant, since willing it would require another will and people cannot dismiss either desire or regret at will.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r3.anchor: قال أصحابنا قوله : { عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم } صريح في أن التوبة لا تحصل إلا من خلق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites interpret God’s repentance as His accepting the servant’s repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r4.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : المراد من قوله : يتوب الله أنه يقبل توبته

RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r5.claim: Razi rejects the Muʿtazilite interpretation: departing from the apparent meaning is warranted only when proof makes it impossible, whereas reason here supports the apparent reading.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140/r5.anchor: والجواب : أن الصرف عن الظاهر إنما يحسن ، إذا ثبت بالدليل أنه لا يمكن إجراء اللفظ على ظاهره

RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r1.claim: Their confession occurred in the past, while the hoped-for repentance is future; confession therefore preceded and was not itself repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r1.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن ذلك الاعتراف ما كان نفس التوبة ، بل كان مقدمة للتوبة ، وأن التوبة إنما تحصل بعدها

BURHAN:v3p130/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p130/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p130/r6.claim: The omitted prepositions reverse the complement order: they mixed righteous deeds with bad ones, and at other times repaired sin by repentance.
BURHAN:v3p130/r6.anchor: اصل الكلام خلطوا عملا صالحا بسيء وآخر سيئا بصالح لأن الخلط يستدعي مخلوط ومخلوطا به
